notes.source: MTG Arena Zone (j2sjosh): Star Trek mechanics preview and set review, Oct-Nov 2026. Summarized; the grades on this site are the model's, not his.
format: Take fixing early: the Planets, shocklands and surveil lands, plus the basic landcyclers (Free Borg Revolutionaries, Humpback Whales, Rogue Artificial Intelligence, Horta, Cold-Blooded Crew). The Strange New Worlds drafters want the same lands, so don't count on them wheeling.

The set is full of 1/1 Officer, Borg and Klingon tokens. X/1 creatures trade with free bodies, edicts usually hit a token (prefer the nontoken ones: In the Pale Moonlight, The Wrath of Khan), and small sweepers like Encounter the Unknown and D'Ghor Bloodletter gain value.
Those same tokens are resources: sacrifice fodder for Eject the Warp Core and Dahar Master, and bodies to station Spacecraft with.
Lots of artifact creatures (Borg, Spacecraft): removal that only hits nonartifact creatures (Resistance Is Futile) is weaker than it looks, and artifact removal (Perils of the Past) has real targets.
Synergy cards are everywhere, but judge each card by what it does without its friends. A deck of weak enablers that say "choose one" or carry the right creature type loses to a deck of good cards.
The colorless Anomaly lands make your colors worse for a late-game bonus; most decks skip them (Gaseous Anomaly is the best of them). Starfleet Academy: never.
Five- and six-drops are crowded with merely fine creatures. Cheap plays that do something are scarcer, and the format's speed is unknown before release.

mechanics.Beam Me Up: Cast the spell from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to your hand, then exile it. Best with creatures that have enters-the-battlefield abilities, which you get to use again; at instant speed it also saves a creature from removal. The price is tempo: picking up your own creature hurts when you're behind or trying to race. Marooned's creature can't be beamed away.
mechanics.Face a Dilemma: Triggers whenever you choose a mode, even an obvious one; choosing several modes on one spell still counts once. Dimir's theme. It works when the modal spells are ones you'd play anyway (Command Decision, Impossible Choice, Federation Probe), not when you're adding weak ones (Test of Courage, Test of Loyalty) to feed the payoffs.
mechanics.Federation: Counts different creature types among your non-Borg creatures. Creatures with several types count for more; assimilated creatures (now Borg) and changelings count for nothing.
mechanics.Strange New Worlds: Counts lands with different names, not colors. Dual lands, Planets, surveil lands and Unexplored Territory (keep it on the battlefield) raise it; Xenobotanist fixes colors but doesn't count. Don't play off-color basics to raise the number.
mechanics.Spacecraft and Station: Tap another creature, even one with summoning sickness, at sorcery speed to add charge counters equal to its power; bigger creatures station faster. Strong when you're ahead, slow when you're behind. The best ships pay you before they're fully stationed (U.S.S. Enterprise-D, U.S.S. Discovery, U.S.S. Enterprise-A).
mechanics.Assimilate: Takes control of a creature, which becomes a Borg artifact creature with a +1/+1 counter. Only on a few mythics so far.
